title: Customer safe-mode communications and recovery options
content:
One-line summary:
We briefly toggled 'tenant safe-mode' for a subset of customers in us-west-2 to contain an unexpected inference degradation (elevated tail latency + occasional truncated structured outputs). This doc provides: (1) two short status-page-ready updates, (2) a customer-facing postmortem draft, (3) recover/replay options we can present for affected tenants, and (4) next steps and internal owners for closure.

Purpose and audience:
Primary: customer success leads who will send status updates and runbooks for customers affected by the event. Secondary: SRE and product owners who need to verify the wording and confirm the technical promises (replay options, data integrity). This is a working draft, not the final legal/finance SLA language.

Affected cohort and impact (summary):
- Time window: 2026-08-03 22:17 UTC -> safe-mode enabled at 2026-08-03 22:45 UTC; partial mitigation by 2026-08-04 03:10 UTC; full normal routing restored 2026-08-05 09:03 UTC.
- Region: us-west-2 (primary). A small fraction of tenants routed through a degraded kernel selection experienced: high 95/99th percentile latency spikes (2x–6x baseline) and intermittent structured output truncation for streaming responses.
- Customer-visible symptoms: slower responses, occasional truncated JSON outputs in streaming sessions, and a small increase in 5xx errors for certain long-context requests. No data corruption detected.
- Affected: ~72 tenants (mix of PLG and enterprise), ~0.9% of total requests during the window.

What we changed (safe-mode explanation for customers):
We activated an automated per-tenant "safe-mode" routing rule that temporarily diverted affected tenants to smaller, more conservative model kernels and reduced max-concurrency for their requests. The goal was to stop progressive degradation and preserve overall correctness while we investigated. Safe-mode preserves customer request semantics (no truncation of stored logs), but can increase per-request latency or reduce throughput.

Short status page updates (concise — for Status Page copy)
1) Initial (to publish at incident start):
Title: Partial latency and structured-output degradation in us-west-2 (some tenants)
Body: We are investigating elevated latency and occasional truncated structured outputs for requests routed through us-west-2. Affected tenants may experience slower responses or incomplete streaming outputs. We have implemented a temporary routing protection (tenant safe-mode) to reduce impact while we investigate. No customer data loss detected. Updates will follow.
2) Progress update (after safe-mode engaged and mitigations confirming progress):
Title: Mitigation applied — tenant safe-mode active; partial recovery ongoing
Body: We have engaged tenant safe-mode for affected tenants and are observing a reduction in error rates. Some tenants will continue to see increased response times as traffic is gradually rebalanced; structured streaming truncations have dropped significantly. We continue validating integrity and will post a detailed postmortem when complete.

Customer-facing postmortem draft (longer form)
Headline: Post-incident summary — temporary routing protection (tenant safe-mode) enabled for a subset of tenants in us-west-2
TL;DR: A kernel selection regression combined with a runtime memory-pressure signal caused the serving runtime to occasionally evict KV cache earlier than intended, which led to increased token-generation latency and, in edge cases, truncated streaming structured outputs. We enabled per-tenant safe-mode to preserve correctness and limit blast radius. No customer data was lost; we are offering replay assistance and a tiered remediation plan for affected tenants.

Root cause (plain language):
During a background kernel swap rollout on 2026-08-03, an interaction between the new kernel's memory accounting and an aggressive cache-eviction heuristic introduced by a runtime tuning change caused the runtime to prematurely evict prefix/KV cache for long-context requests. When cache was evicted mid-generation, some streaming sessions hit a path that truncated the structured output buffer instead of seamlessly re-requesting missing KV entries. This was more likely under certain long-context patterns and at high concurrency.

Why it affected customers:
- Tenants with many long-context streams (system+user+tool calls) were more likely to hit the bug.
- The kernel rollout targeted a small batch of hosts in us-west-2, so customer impact was regionally concentrated.
- Our fallback and retry thresholds were insufficiently conservative for this pattern, so the degradation cascaded into higher latencies rather than graceful retries.

Mitigation timeline (concise):
- 2026-08-03 21:48 UTC: monitoring alerts triggered (95th/99th latency rising).
- 2026-08-03 22:12 UTC: SRE triage identified correlation with a kernel swap PR (PR#72).
- 2026-08-03 22:17 UTC: incremental rollbacks and increased cache-protection flags started on canary hosts.
- 2026-08-03 22:45 UTC: tenant safe-mode policy deployed for affected tenants (automated per-tenant routing).
- 2026-08-04 03:10 UTC: error rates decreased; structured truncations near zero for safe-mode tenants.
- 2026-08-05 09:03 UTC: full rollback completed; normal routing restored after extended validation.

Data integrity and customer assurances:
- We have verified logs and persisted request traces; there is no evidence of lost or corrupted customer data.
- Streaming truncations were returned to the client at the time; the request logs show the original inputs and partial outputs.
- For customers requesting re-generation of affected requests, we can offer a targeted replay service (see options below).

Customer options (what we can offer customers and sample wording to send):
1) Automated replay assistance (recommended for applications that rely on complete structured streaming outputs):
- What we do: We will re-run affected requests against a validated baseline kernel in a secure, read-only replay job and provide regenerated outputs for your validation. We do not re-send outputs to end-users unless you ask.
- Expected timeline: batch replays will start within 72 hours of request and complete within 5 business days for small to medium queues; enterprise scale may vary.
- How to request: reply to this notification or open a support ticket with tag "replay-request-INC-4987".
2) Opt-in fast-rollforward (for customers that want low-latency normal routing as soon as safe kernel changes are validated):
- What we do: with your consent we will fast-forward your tenant out of safe-mode to the validated kernel under a canary policy that limits concurrency and enables accelerated monitoring. This is an opt-in process.
- Risk: small chance of re-exposure if the kernel path still has edge cases; we will not fast-forward without explicit customer approval.
3) SLA / credit discussion:
- We will provide a tailored SLA impact summary and propose credits for tenants with measurable customer impact. Finance and legal will follow-up for enterprise accounts.

Suggested customer-facing FAQ snippets (short answers)
Q: Did you lose my data?
A: No — we have validated that no customer data was lost or corrupted. Logs and request traces are intact.
Q: Why did my responses get slower?
A: We temporarily routed some tenants into a conservative execution path to stop the progressive degradation; this preserves correctness but can increase latency for certain request shapes.
Q: Can you re-generate the responses my users saw?
A: Yes — we offer a replay service for affected requests. Please open a support ticket and include any request IDs or sample timestamps.

Internal action items and owners (for closure):
- Engineering (Model Serving) — PR rollback postmortem and guarded rollout strategy (owner: Diego Morales) — due 2026-08-10.
- Runtime team — add defensive check that prevents truncation path when KV eviction occurs mid-generation; write unit+integration tests (owner: Marcus Chen) — due 2026-08-12.
- SRE — audit auto-rollback thresholds and improve observability for early cache-eviction signals (owner: Priya Kapoor) — due 2026-08-11.
- Customer Success — outreach sweep to affected tenants, provide replay opt-in forms and SLA impact notes (owner: Aisha Patel) — outreach start 2026-08-06.

Template customer outreach (email / post):
Subject: Update: temporary routing protection engaged for some requests in us-west-2
Body (concise): Hi — we wanted to let you know we observed elevated latency and intermittent truncated streaming outputs for some requests in us-west-2 on 2026-08-03. We engaged a per-tenant safe-mode to contain the issue and rolled back the kernel change; normal service was restored 2026-08-05 after validation. No customer data was lost. If you would like us to replay affected requests or opt-in for a fast rollforward, please reply or open a support ticket with tag "replay-request-INC-4987".

Open questions / risks to discuss with product/legal:
- Standardizing replay SLAs and data retention for replays (how long we keep request bodies for replay consent).
- Credit policy language for PLG versus enterprise tiers that were affected by safe-mode changes.

Appendix: diagnostic artifacts we will attach to customer packages
- Evidence bundle (redacted) showing request IDs, timestamps, and before/after outputs.
- Short log extracts demonstrating cache eviction signals and the kernel mismatch trace.
- Link to internal RCA (Confluence) and PR (GitHub).

Draft next message to publish to status page and customer email should be reviewed by CS lead and engineering before sending. This doc is intended to be the single source for comms drafts and customer-choice options for INC-4987.

Notes to self (working):
- Confirm exact tenant list for targeted outreach with billing (privacy-safe).
- Confirm replay storage window (how old requests we can reasonably replay).
- Coordinate a single owner for completed evidence bundles per customer to avoid duplication.

End of draft.
